name: Now You Don't
flavor: The curtain drops for exactly one second. When it rises, you're not where the audience is looking anymore.
description: You vanish behind a snap of silk and misdirection, becoming invisible until the start of your next turn or until you make an attack roll, force a saving throw, or force an ability check, whichever comes first. As part of casting this, you may also move up to 10 feet without provoking opportunity attacks — the last thing anyone saw of you was already the wrong direction. This is misdirection, not true invisibility, and it can be beaten by simply watching you properly: each creature that can see you at the moment you cast it makes a Wisdom (Perception) check against your {{trick save DC|8 + proficiency bonus + your trick ability modifier}}. On a success that creature tracks where you actually went and you are not invisible to it — though you remain invisible to every creature that failed, and to anything that could not see you cast it.
narration: The curtain drops for exactly one second. When it lifts you are not where anyone is looking — and the only ones who find you are the ones who were watching your feet instead of your hands.
sheetSummary: Bonus action, self, cooldown 3. Invisible until the start of your next turn or until you attack or force a save or check; may move 10 ft without provoking as part of the trick. Each creature that can SEE you cast it makes a Wisdom (Perception) check vs {{trick save DC|8 + proficiency bonus + your trick ability modifier}}; on a success it tracks you and you are not invisible to that creature.
